name: @equaltoai/contentus
description: Contentus — the FaceTheory + greater-components CMS client installed into lesser instances.

scripts.build:assets: node scripts/copy-facetheory-manifest.mjs && node scripts/build-stylesheet.mjs && node scripts/copy-brand-assets.mjs
scripts.build: pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run svelte-check && pnpm run build:client && pnpm run build:server && pnpm run build:assets && pnpm run validate
scripts.validate: pnpm run validate:graphql && pnpm run validate:renderer-authority && pnpm run validate:csp && pnpm run validate:seam-graph

comments.renderer_authority: Contentus ships NO Markdown rendering pipeline. lesser's server-side renderer/sanitizer (pkg/cmsrender) is the single authority for article HTML. The `unified`/`rehype-*`/`hast-util-sanitize` deps are present for exactly one reason: the vendored greater blog face's Article.Content imports `sanitizeHtml` from src/lib/greater/utils, which is greater's HTML SANITIZER (defence-in-depth over lesser's authority) — not a renderer. The Markdown RENDERING chain (remark-parse, remark-gfm, remark-rehype, mdast-*, shiki) is deliberately absent: the only vendored files that need it are MarkdownRenderer.svelte, html-to-markdown.ts, and CodeBlock.svelte, none of which contentus imports. `scripts/audit-renderer-authority.mjs` enforces both halves of this line on every build. See docs/consumption/renderer-authority.md.
comments.greater_cli_findings: Two `greater` CLI defects hit during the M1 vendoring at greater-v0.11.9, both routed upstream rather than worked around: (1) `greater add` rewrote contentus-owned package.json devDependencies to nonexistent versions (vite ^10.0.1, @types/node ^3.1.0, @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte ^10.1.2, typescript ^6.0.0, svelte-check ^9.0.1, prettier ^2.1.2) and replaced the pinned greater-components-adapters tarball with the nonexistent range ^11.0.5 — package.json is contentus-owned, so it was restored, not patched around; (2) vendored source is emitted with bare, unresolvable specifiers (`from 'src/lib/greater/utils'`) in 65 files — the CLI substitutes the components.json alias TARGET instead of an alias-prefixed path. Fixed host-side with a resolve alias in vite.config.ts and tsconfig.json paths; no vendored file was hand-edited. BOTH REPRODUCE AT greater-v0.12.0 (M2d pin bump), which is what makes them standing defects rather than one bad build: #918 emitted a fresh set of nonexistent ranges (prettier ^10.1.2, typescript ^3.1.0, vite ^2.1.2, @types/node ^0.14.0, @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte ^3.2.0, svelte-check ^4.0.9) and again replaced every greater tarball pin with an invented semver range (adapters ^16.12.0, headless ^2.47.14, icons ^3.19.0, primitives ^6.0.6, tokens ^11.0.0, utils ^4.0.1) — a manifest no `--frozen-lockfile` install can resolve. It also ADDED the Markdown rendering chain contentus refuses (remark-parse, remark-gfm, remark-rehype, mdast-util-*, hast-util-to-mdast, shiki) plus Apollo, graphql, and viem as direct dependencies. The manifest was restored from the pre-run copy and only the greater tarball URLs were moved to 0.12.0 by hand; `pnpm install` then pruned the additions, and the renderer-authority audit is what proves the Markdown chain did not survive. THIRD REPRODUCTION AT M4 (face 4 vendoring, greater-v0.12.0, same pinned CLI 0.12.0): #918 again rewrote devDependencies to nonexistent ranges (@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte ^10.1.2, @types/node ^3.1.0, prettier ^2.1.2) and again added thirteen dependencies NOTHING in the vendored tree imports — the Markdown rendering chain contentus refuses (remark-parse, remark-gfm, remark-rehype, mdast-util-gfm, mdast-util-to-markdown, hast-util-to-mdast, shiki) plus @apollo/client, @apollo/client-react-streaming, @graphql-typed-document-node/core, graphql and viem. The dependency list is a union of registry metadata, not a function of the emitted imports: walking every bare specifier in the files this run wrote yields exactly ONE external package, @tanstack/svelte-virtual. The manifest was restored from the pre-run copy and only that one dependency was added by hand; `pnpm install` then pruned the other twelve, and the renderer-authority audit is what proves the Markdown chain did not survive. #919 did NOT bite this time: the bare `@equaltoai/greater-components/*` specifiers in the face-4 tree all sit inside `@example` doc comments, not in executable import statements, so the existing resolve alias was not extended.
comments.greater_update_prune: THE FOURTH CLI FINDING FROM M2, AND IT CLOSED RATHER THAN OPENED. At the 0.13.0 pin the `social-timeline` registry entry emitted two files into the consumer's own `lib` alias — src/lib/lesserTimelineStore.ts and src/lib/lesserTimelineStore.svelte.ts — which contentus imports nowhere, and the managed channel had no operation that could take them back: the 0.13.0 CLI registers init, add, list, diff, update, doctor, audit, cache, with no remove, no uninstall, and no prune on `update`. Hand-deleting vendored bytes is the edit this repository refuses, and removing the whole entry was not correct either, because contentus BUILDS src/lib/components/TimelineVirtualized.svelte from the same atomic entry. So the files stayed, declared. greater-v0.13.1 (upstream #1000/#1001) withdrew exactly those two paths from the `social-timeline` entry and taught `greater update` to prune a managed file the registry no longer owns, deriving ownership from every registry category so over-inclusion can only ever PROTECT a path. Verified against this consumer with the digest-verified released CLI: `greater update --all --ref greater-v0.13.1 --dry-run` reported 'social-timeline: 6 updated, 6 unchanged, 2 to prune' naming both files and changed nothing; the real run reported '2 pruned' and git shows exactly two deletions and zero source modifications. TimelineVirtualized.svelte, TimelineVirtualizedReactive.svelte and src/lib/components/messaging/sanitize.ts are all retained. AND THE MANIFEST DEFECT DID NOT REPRODUCE: package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml were byte-identical before and after the run, compared against a pre-run snapshot. That is a statement about `update`, not an all-clear for `add` — #918 was only ever observed on `greater add`, which this milestone did not run. The tarball pins and the graphql devDependency in this manifest were moved by hand, deliberately, as contentus-owned manifest policy. components.json now records 1119 per-file checksums; all 1119 were independently recomputed from the bytes on disk and matched, with no entry marked modified.
comments.timeline_dependencies: Face 4 added exactly ONE runtime dependency, and the one it did not add is the more interesting half. `@tanstack/svelte-virtual` is imported directly by the vendored `TimelineVirtualized.svelte` and `TimelineVirtualizedReactive.svelte`; walking every bare specifier in the files the M4 `greater add` run wrote yields that package and nothing else. `graphql-ws` was NOT added, deliberately. lesser documents `graphql-transport-ws` as the subscription protocol and names that npm package in its example (docs/api-reference.md -> 'GraphQL subscriptions (WebSocket)'), so declaring it looked like the contract-following move. It is not, and the reason that still holds is the small one: contentus needs a few hundred bytes of the protocol, not a client library, and a smaller surface is a smaller thing to get wrong. HISTORICAL, AND NO LONGER A REASON: at M4 declaring it also hoisted a second copy of `ws` and MOVED the SEC-2 advisory path then pinned in gov-infra/planning/contentus-disclosed-upstream-findings.json from `.>@equaltoai/greater-components-adapters>graphql-ws>ws` to `.>@equaltoai/greater-components-adapters>viem>ws` — perturbing an open high-severity advisory's disclosed shape to add a client nothing needed. That advisory (GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p) was RETIRED at the greater-v0.13.0 pin bump, whose adapters resolve ws@8.21.0, and the SEC-2 disclosed set is now EMPTY; the decision stands on its own merits rather than on an advisory that no longer exists. So `src/lib/timelines/subscription.ts` speaks the documented graphql-transport-ws framing over the browser's native WebSocket instead. This is the same call `src/lib/cms/graphql.ts` already makes against Apollo for queries, for the same stated reason: contentus needs the protocol, not a client library, and a smaller surface is a smaller thing to get wrong. Speaking a documented wire protocol is not inventing a transport; the endpoint, subprotocol, and auth placement all come from lesser's contract. The vendored `src/lib/transport.ts` is unused for a different reason - it speaks Mastodon's `/api/v1/streaming` subscribe-frame protocol, which is lesser's OTHER realtime surface (`wss://ws.<domain>/stream`), not the GraphQL subscription endpoint face 4 is specified against. See docs/consumption/timeline-contract.md.
comments.greater_channels: Two upstream-sanctioned channels, both `greater` CLI managed, pinned in lockstep to greater-v0.13.5 (vendored_ref 6374ce9f8461c4dbbf529491d01db1b534144ffb): (1) TARBALL-PIN for compiled sub-packages imported as npm modules; (2) CLI-COPY (`installMode: vendored`) for faces and shared modules, recorded in components.json. Vendored source is never hand-edited — updates flow through the CLI, and gov-infra/verifiers/check-greater-pins.mjs fails if the two channels name different refs. EVERY BUMP MOVES BOTH CHANNELS IN ONE COMMIT, because CON-4 requires it: every components.json `installed[]` entry must carry the pinned `vendored_ref`, so the whole vendored tree is re-emitted by the CLI rather than one module being added at a newer ref. History: the M2d bump from 0.11.9 to 0.12.0 was forced by face 2's review chrome (the `review` registry entry exists only from greater-v0.12.0); the M6 bump to 0.13.0 was forced by the messaging faces' rendering fixes and by the lesser v1.6.0 article-tombstone contract; the M2 bump to 0.13.1 was forced by PRUNING — see greater_update_prune; the audit-remediation bump to 0.13.2 was forced by lesser v1.6.2's canonical `Article.renderedHtml`, which 0.13.2's blog normalization consumes (upstream #1005), and by its FaceTheory v4.0.6 sync.
comments.facetheory_pin: FaceTheory v4.0.9 release tarball. v4.0.9 is the AppTheory v4.1.0-aligned release: FaceTheory's own devDependencies move to apptheory 4.1.0 / apptheory-cdk 4.1.0 / tabletheory-ts 3.0.6 (plus the matching pnpm override), runtime dependencies remain zero, and peerDependencies are unchanged. UNLIKE v4.0.7 (dev-tree-only, byte-identical dist), v4.0.9 ships real DIST changes, confined to the navigation-pending and control-plane modules: navigation-pending gains the additive NAVIGATION_PENDING_FORM_OPT_OUT_ATTRIBUTE ('data-facetheory-no-pending') and moves form pending activation to a post-dispatch microtask (queueMicrotask -> Promise -> setTimeout fallback), skipping preventDefault-ed submits, opted-out forms, and submits that never navigate this document (method='dialog', non-_self formtarget); the pending mark no longer writes aria-busy='true' onto app-owned nodes (observe-only posture — the accessible signal is the framework-owned indicator pill). The control-plane stylesheet's pending-control selector moves from .facetheory-navigation-pending-control[aria-busy='true'] to .facetheory-navigation-pending-control[data-facetheory-navigation-pending]. AUDIT — contentus consumes NONE of this surface: it imports neither navigation-pending nor control-plane (src/facetheory/entry-server.ts imports the SSR/CSP/asset surface only), startNavigationPending is called nowhere, and the shipped stylesheet (scripts/build-stylesheet.mjs) assembles greater-components and contentus brand layers only, so no FaceTheory control-plane CSS ships. Every aria-busy usage in src/ sits on contentus's own components (TimelineVirtualized, AgentSharingPanel, auth cards) or vendored greater components (Button/Avatar/LoadingState/CommandPalette/face Roots), each styled independently; grep across src/, tests/, and scripts/ finds zero references to .facetheory-navigation-pending*. NO ADAPTATION WAS REQUIRED. The tarball sha256 ed8c9c69c0dd7dc12a7ae4018678bd482eb15487d62100faa1f16f8e3520e2d2 matches the release's official SHA256SUMS.txt asset, and `pnpm audit` is clean across the whole graph on the new lockfile, so the SEC-2 disclosed set stays empty — INTENTIONALLY (examined, not skipped). v4.0.8, published in between, is not adopted here because this wave's target is the AppTheory-v4.1.0-aligned release, which is v4.0.9. This pin sits three patches AHEAD of the v4.0.6 that BOTH lesser's CLIENT_APP_GUIDE.md (docs/guides/CLIENT_APP_GUIDE.md, verified at lesser staging 3b79aa61318d81af4140375da9d1f78a01277789) still recommends as the current release pin AND greater-v0.13.5 itself pins upstream — deliberate: the dist delta is real but audited as unconsumed, the guide explicitly permits 'an explicitly reviewed newer FaceTheory release' for operator releases, and `lesser client install` validates only that @theory-cloud/facetheory is present, so v4.0.9 satisfies the install contract either way.
